key_insight: TAPESTRY makes 45,430 recurrent tumor-enriched splice junctions searchable to help prioritize potential immunotherapy targets in pediatric brain tumors.
clinical_relevance: Splice-derived targets could expand immunotherapy research opportunities in tumors with few mutation-derived neoantigens, but clinical benefit is not established.
method: Compare tumor RNA-seq with four normal brain reference cohorts to identify tumor-enriched junctions.
Classify junctions as tumor-specific or oncofetal and annotate recurrence, coding consequences and protein-domain overlap.
Provide interactive search, visualization, downloads and a documented REST API.
evidence_signal: The resource catalogs junctions across 19 histologies using 1,962 RNA-seq specimens, including 1,272 independent primary tumors, with adult, pediatric, developmental and cell-type-resolved normal brain references.
watch_item: RNA-level enrichment alone does not establish protein production, immune accessibility or therapeutic safety; these require experimental validation.
paper_title: TAPESTRY: an interactive resource for exploring tumor-enriched splice junctions in pediatric brain tumors
